title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer thresholds and stabilize regional failover/hysteresis
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Context: During an incident on 2026-02-08 we observed repeated regional failovers when the SLO enforcer aggressively started load-shedding under transient latency spikes. Root cause: hysteresis on the per-region circuit-breaker counters was too short and our node-state transition was not atomic across the controller/listener, which could lead to brief over-shedding and immediate failover to other regions, causing thrash. This hotfix tightens thresholds, adds stronger hysteresis, and makes the node state transitions atomic to avoid races.

What this PR does: - Tighten SLO enforcer thresholds and increase backoff window for region-level circuit breakers. - Add a hysteresis counter with min-duration enforcement (region stays in degraded state for N seconds once tripped). - Replace non-atomic state updates with CAS-backed update path in services/slo-enforcer/state.go to prevent double-shedding races. - Add metrics and debug logs to track per-region trip counts and recovery durations. - Include integration test that simulates transient latency spikes and asserts no >1 failover within a 60s window. - Helm values bump with conservative defaults and a migration comment for Dedicated clusters.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added/updated [x] Integration test added [x] Metrics and dashboards updated [x] Rollback plan documented

Motivation: Reduce customer-visible failovers and avoid cascading capacity loss during short-lived infra noise. This is a minimal-risk hotfix targeted at the enforcer control loop; no changes to user-facing API paths.

Rollback plan: Revert this branch (hotfix/slo-enforcer-regional-thresholds-118888). If accidental regression observed, we can flip feature flag slo_enforcer_hysteresis.enabled to false via console/values.

Related: ENG-6721 (investigation), SUP-3478 (customer escalations).
